title: Minimax Estimation of Wasserstein-One Treatment Contrasts with Laplace Error and Outcome Validation
banked_reason: The delivered contribution is the matched scalar-functional frontier for this fixed Laplace-error validation experiment; the supplied polynomial and marked-mixture proofs discharge the bottlenecks described as unresolved in the brief. The logarithmic gains extend established nonsmooth-norm machinery, while the cited [recovery theorem](https://doi.org/10.1007/s10260-026-00858-9) concerns whole-law loss and does not subsume the mixed scalar result. The TL;DR's matched-rate and validation-budget claims are consistent with the supplied arguments, with no identified stale conjectural overclaim. However, at r=0 the attaining estimator is identically 1/2 below the astronomical threshold ceil(exp(8000000)), and the package supplies no computational demonstration that the scalar correction improves useful finite-sample performance. The narrowly specified experiment and unusable numerical guarantees constrain the leading-journal significance and projected score despite the completed rate characterization. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

proof_attempt_summary: Discovery completed the claimed joint scalar risk/honest-length frontier and validation-budget characterization over the fixed Laplace-error parent, with clean decision/math reviews and five source attestations. The field significance requirement failed because the numerical threshold is astronomical and the package lacks useful-sample computational validation in a narrow experiment. The independent terminal-validity audit confirmed no bounded within-topic field repair; Lean formalization was not launched and no Lean proof or reusable verified substrate is claimed.
tldr: For the scalar first-Wasserstein contrast under known Laplace assay error and a fixed accurate-outcome subsample, the minimax absolute-risk and finite 90 percent honest connected-length frontiers coincide, up to explicit universal constants, at \(\min\{1,n^{-1/2}+\min[(n\log(en))^{-2/7},n^{-1/8}(r+1)^{-3/8}/\sqrt{\log(e+n/(r+1))}]\}\). A total local-moment estimator and interval attain this rate on the full compact zero-extended \(H^1\) parent, while compact marked likelihood mixtures give the matching original-record converse. The noisy/mixed transition occurs at \(r+1\asymp n^{3/7}[\log(en)]^{-4/7}\), and uniform root-n precision holds exactly when \(r_n=\Omega(n)\).
gap: Whole-law Wasserstein deconvolution and direct-Gaussian norm estimation do not establish sharp scalar-distance complexity when accurate outcomes and Laplace surrogates coexist in a fixed marked experiment.
fill: Open-ended Question 1 requires a public evaluated frontier, total attaining procedures and original-record scalar converses. Theorem 1 separately constrains root-n validation budgets without assuming the unresolved logarithmic answer.
